natural: rob the rich to help the poor

meaning.en: To take from the rich to help the poor.
meaning.zh: 夺取富人的财物去救济穷人。

equivalents: rob the rich to give to the poor

examples.zh: 传说中的侠盗专门劫富济贫。
examples.en: The legendary outlaw was said to rob the rich to feed the poor.

examples.zh: 电影讲的是一群劫富济贫的好汉。
examples.en: The film is about a band of heroes who steal from the rich to help the poor.

meaning.en: To judge people's feelings from their words and expressions.
meaning.zh: 观察别人的言语和脸色，来揣摩对方的心意。

equivalents: size people up by their expression

examples.zh: 做销售要学会察言观色。
examples.en: In sales you must learn to read your customers.

examples.zh: 这孩子从小就会察言观色。
examples.en: The child has known how to read people since small.

usage.zh: 多作谓语，有时略带贬义。

meaning.en: Captivating; making one yearn for it.
meaning.zh: 使人心里十分向往。

examples.zh: 那片雪山风光令人神往。
examples.en: The snowy mountain scenery is captivating.

examples.zh: 他描绘的未来令人神往。
examples.en: The future he painted was enticing.

meaning.en: Stuffed full and bulging.
meaning.zh: 形容口袋、包等塞得满满的，向外凸出。

examples.zh: 他的书包鼓鼓囊囊的。
examples.en: His schoolbag was bulging.

examples.zh: 衣兜里鼓鼓囊囊塞满了糖果。
examples.en: His pockets were stuffed to bursting with sweets.

meaning.en: Barren land where nothing grows.
meaning.zh: 寸草不生的荒地。

examples.zh: 他们把不毛之地变成了绿洲。
examples.en: They turned barren wasteland into an oasis.

examples.zh: 这里曾是一片不毛之地。
examples.en: This was once a barren waste.

story.en: In the Gongyang Commentary's account of King Zhuang of Chu's siege of Zheng, the Lord of Zheng offers to be sent away to a barren land (不毛之地). The term for land where nothing grows comes from this passage.
story.zh: 《公羊传·宣公十二年》载楚庄王围郑，郑伯请求“锡之不毛之地”，后以“不毛之地”指寸草不生的荒地。

literal: since · wrong · go along with · wrong

meaning.en: To carry on with a mistake rather than correct it.
meaning.zh: 事情已经错了，索性顺着错的继续做下去。

equivalents: make the best of a mistake

examples.zh: 既然订错了票，我们就将错就错，换个地方玩。
examples.en: Since we booked the wrong tickets, we rolled with it and went somewhere else.

examples.zh: 他将错就错，把错别字当成了笔名。
examples.en: He ran with the typo and used it as a pen name.

meaning.en: To long for someone or something day and night.
meaning.zh: 魂魄被牵挂，梦中也萦绕，形容思念深切。

examples.zh: 故乡的一草一木让他魂牵梦萦。
examples.en: Every blade of grass back home haunts his dreams.

examples.zh: 这位歌手让万千粉丝魂牵梦萦。
examples.en: The singer has thousands of fans pining for her.

meaning.en: One's best-known skill or party piece.
meaning.zh: 最擅长的本领或技艺。

examples.zh: 做红烧肉是他的拿手好戏。
examples.en: Braised pork is his signature dish.

examples.zh: 唱京剧可是她的拿手好戏。
examples.en: Singing Peking opera is her forte.

usage.en: Object; often 是…的拿手好戏.

natural: every trade has its top talent

meaning.en: In every line of work one can reach the top.
meaning.zh: 不论哪一行，都能出顶尖人才。

equivalents: you can excel in any field

examples.zh: 行行出状元，不必都挤着考大学。
examples.en: Every trade has its star; not everyone has to crowd into university.

examples.zh: 他做木工做成了名家，真是行行出状元。
examples.en: He became a master carpenter: proof that every trade has its champions.

synonyms: 天生我材必有用，千金散尽还复来
variants: 三百六十行，行行出状元

meaning.en: Clear knowledge of one's own strengths and limits.
meaning.zh: 正确认识自己的能力和不足。

examples.zh: 他很有自知之明，从不勉强自己。
examples.en: He has self-awareness and never overreaches.

examples.zh: 你要有点自知之明。
examples.en: You should know your own limits.

usage.en: Object; often 有/缺乏自知之明.
usage.zh: 常作宾语，如“有自知之明”。

antonyms: 乌鸦站在猪身上——光看见别人黑
小娃娃扛大梁——自不量力
癞蛤蟆想吃天鹅肉——痴心妄想

meaning.en: To choose words and sentences with great care.
meaning.zh: 对每个字每句话都认真推敲。

examples.zh: 这份声明他字斟句酌，改了十几遍。
examples.en: He weighed every word of the statement and revised it a dozen times.

examples.zh: 写合同要字斟句酌。
examples.en: Contracts need every word weighed.

meaning.en: Joking, laughing, raging and cursing; a lively range of expression.
meaning.zh: 嬉笑和怒骂，泛指各种情绪表现，也形容文章或言论生动犀利。

equivalents: a mix of jest and invective

examples.zh: 他的杂文嬉笑怒骂，皆成文章。
examples.en: His essays, jesting and scolding alike, all become literature.

examples.zh: 舞台上嬉笑怒骂，演尽人生百态。
examples.en: On stage, with laughter and anger, they play out every side of life.

natural: kill two birds with one stone

meaning.en: To achieve two aims with a single action.
meaning.zh: 一支箭射中两只雕，比喻做一件事达到两个目的。

equivalents: kill two birds with one stone

examples.zh: 利用周末做志愿者，既锻炼了自己又帮了别人，一箭双雕。
examples.en: Volunteering at weekends trains me and helps others: two birds with one stone.

examples.zh: 这一招一箭双雕。
examples.en: This move kills two birds with one stone.

story.en: The Northern History tells how Changsun Sheng, given two arrows when two eagles fought over meat, pierced both with a single shot, winning fame as a marksman. 一箭双雕 grew from this feat.
story.zh: 《北史·长孙晟传》载：有两雕飞而争肉，长孙晟奉命射之，“一发双贯焉”。后作“一箭双雕”。

meaning.en: The time is not far off.
meaning.zh: 离预定的日期不远了。

examples.zh: 胜利的日子为期不远。
examples.en: The day of victory is not far off.

examples.zh: 新校区建成为期不远。
examples.en: The new campus will be finished before long.

meaning.en: Too impatient to wait.
meaning.zh: 急得不能忍耐，一刻也等不了。

examples.zh: 孩子急不可耐地拆开了礼物。
examples.en: The child tore open the present, unable to wait.

examples.zh: 他急不可耐地想知道结果。
examples.en: He was dying to know the result.

meaning.en: To not shy away from hard work.
meaning.zh: 不怕辛苦，不推辞劳累。

examples.zh: 医生不辞劳苦，连夜赶到现场。
examples.en: The doctor spared no effort and rushed to the scene overnight.

examples.zh: 他不辞劳苦地照顾老人。
examples.en: He tirelessly cared for the elderly.

meaning.en: To discuss things as if on a par; mostly negative: not comparable.
meaning.zh: 把不同的人或事放在一起谈论、相提并论；多用否定。

examples.zh: 今日的生活与往昔不可同日而语。
examples.en: Life today cannot be mentioned in the same breath as the past.

examples.zh: 两者的质量不能同日而语。
examples.en: The two are not comparable in quality.

usage.en: Mostly negated: 不可/不能同日而语.

meaning.en: One of the few valuable things left.
meaning.zh: 大果子只剩下少数几个，比喻稀少而珍贵的人或事物留存下来。

examples.zh: 这家老字号是当地硕果仅存的手工作坊。
examples.en: This old shop is one of the last handicraft workshops in town.

examples.zh: 他是那一代学者中硕果仅存的一位。
examples.en: He is one of the few left of that generation of scholars.

meaning.en: To have lived through many changes of fortune.
meaning.zh: 经历了许多世事变化。

examples.zh: 老人饱经沧桑，眼神却很平静。
examples.en: The old man has seen much of life, yet his gaze is calm.

examples.zh: 饱经沧桑的古城依然屹立。
examples.en: The ancient city, weathered by the ages, still stands.

meaning.en: To recite fluently, even backwards.
meaning.zh: 形容熟记于心，背得极熟。

examples.zh: 这首诗他早就倒背如流。
examples.en: He has long known the poem by heart.

examples.zh: 这些公式她倒背如流。
examples.en: She knows these formulas backwards.

meaning.en: To scheme against one another.
meaning.zh: 各用心机，互相排挤。

examples.zh: 办公室里勾心斗角，让他心力交瘁。
examples.en: The office intrigue wore him out.

examples.zh: 他们为了职位勾心斗角。
examples.en: They schemed against each other for the post.

story.en: In Du Mu's rhapsody on the Epang Palace, the buildings are described as 'hearts clasping, horns jousting' (钩心斗角): eaves and corners meeting and clashing in intricate design. The sense of scheming against others is a later extension.
story.zh: 杜牧《阿房宫赋》：“廊腰缦回，檐牙高啄；各抱地势，钩心斗角。”原指宫室建筑结构交错精巧，后喻人事上互相算计。

meaning.en: Cooking condiments; the small stuff of daily life.
meaning.zh: 日常做饭用的调料，泛指日常生活琐事。

examples.zh: 过日子就是油盐酱醋。
examples.en: Everyday life is just oil, salt, soy sauce and vinegar.

examples.zh: 他每天操心油盐酱醋，没时间看书。
examples.en: Busy with daily household chores, he has no time to read.

synonyms: 开门七件事，柴米油盐酱醋茶

natural: the true mettle of a hero

meaning.en: The true character of a hero.
meaning.zh: 英雄原有的品质和气概。

examples.zh: 危急关头，他显出了英雄本色。
examples.en: At the crisis he showed a hero's true colours.

examples.zh: 消防员冲进火场，尽显英雄本色。
examples.en: The firefighters rushed in, showing true heroism.

usage.en: Object; often 显出/尽显英雄本色.

literal: take on all · fight · the world

meaning.en: To insist on doing everything oneself.
meaning.zh: 什么事都想一个人包办，不让别人插手。

examples.zh: 领导不能包打天下，要学会授权。
examples.en: A leader can't do everything alone and must learn to delegate.

examples.zh: 他总想包打天下，结果累垮了。
examples.en: He wanted to run the whole show himself and burned out.
